title: Vowels and Consonants
paragraphs: The teacher asked the students in the classroom, “How would you remember the vowels in Tamil?”
“Sir, shall I answer?” said student Maṇivācakaṉ.
“I would remember the twelve-handed Murukaṉ to give me the cue”, pat came the reply.
“Oh, good! You evoke spirituality”, smiled the teacher.
“Sir, kuṟiñci flowers blossom once in twelve years. That would remind me of the twelve vowel letters”, was the reply of Pūṅkōti, a girl student.
The teacher took turns to question a farmer’s son, “O boy! What would you do to remember the vowels?”

“Sir, the month of Thai ushers in the Poṅkal festival which is marked by new clothes, cleaning houses, worshipping paddy and decorating bullocks. After celebrating the festival this year we would have to wait for twelve long months for its recurrence. In the same manner, the twelve vowels would be etched on my mind.”
The teacher posed his next question, “Okay, how would you remember the consonants?”
“The eighteen sacred steps of Lord Sabarimalai Ayyappa shrine would remind me of the eighteen consonants, sir”, was the reply of student Maṇivācakaṉ.

Pūṅkōti got up to speak wisely, “The great Cēra king Ceṅkuṭṭuvaṉ vanquished the Aryan kings Kanaka Vicayar at Kuyilāluvam to get the stone for carving Kaṇṇaki’s statue. He made them carry the stones on their heads. At that juncture, an elated Ceṅkuṭṭuvaṉ roared, ‘The war between gods and demons lasted for eighteen years. The great Rāmāyaṇa war spanned out for eighteen months. The Mahābārata war went on for eighteen days, whereas Cēraṉ Ceṅkuṭṭuvaṉ’s war against the Himalayan kingdom finished within eighteen nāḻikai (one nāḻikai = 24 minutes).’
Since I remember this inspirational speech, the fact that consonants are eighteen would remain deeply embedded in my mind.”
The teacher patted Pūṅkōti proudly and concluded, “Though based on spirituality and rationality, which are poles apart, your answers are appropriate.”
The teacher conveyed his greetings to the students.
> The twelve phonemes (from /a/ through /au/) > Are known to be vowels, > So has it been laid down. > > (Eḻuttatikāram : Nūl Marapu, verse 8)
> The eighteen phonemes (from /k/ through /ṉ/) > Are called consonants, > Thus goes the usage codified. > > (Nūl Marapu, verse 9)
